decisions.place: First entry, abbreviation before de Lefschetz
decisions.scan_shows: The t and h are followed by a gap before de; no separate abbreviation point is present.
The long descending p strokes and the joined o-s-e-r ending are visible in the right half; H uncertainty is not retained.

decisions.place: First entry, connector between X and Y
decisions.scan_shows: After X the ink has a short n-shaped arch followed by an i stroke, not the loop and cross-stroke of et.

A V-shaped pair of converging strokes is strong; a further lighter upright/right limb remains distinguishable but cannot securely be assigned to an independent I rather than retracing. Upper and lower rules are present.
After the a and u, the terminal stroke bends slightly down and stops. There is no independent crossed x before the colon.

decisions.place: Second entry, word immediately after colon
decisions.scan_shows: The beginning has a small isolated upright/curved group, a detached dot, and a loop with a long leftward descender; the later tall ascender has no decisive crossbar. This favours signaler, but the reduced joins still permit rajouter.
The initial r-a-i-s, a looped o, the two low n groups, an a loop, and the two tall b/l strokes with the final tail can be followed in the crop.

Upper and lower horizontal rules and portions of upright and converging strokes survive several heavy diagonal cancellation strokes. IV is the best partial reading, but the cancellation prevents deciding it over V or VI.

decisions.place: Third entry, replacement VI and enclosing stroke
decisions.scan_shows: The replacement VI is physically below the blackened numeral. A single U-like stroke descends beside its left edge, passes below it, and rises farther on the right toward the old numeral. The reading stacks the replacement below the cancellation. H gives only a prose description of this placement.
The right half shows a short rising then crossing terminal stroke after the u, before the page margin; the x is present.
The first character is a closed low oval, followed by a shallow u-shaped join; no t ascender or crossbar occurs in this word.

decisions.place: Third entry, small mark above ou
decisions.scan_shows: The raised mark has crossing diagonals and a faint further lateral arm. An asterisk is favoured over a plus, but the short faint arms do not fully settle the glyph.

decisions.place: Third entry, mark after opening parenthesis
decisions.scan_shows: A separate dark head with a narrow downward taper lies between the opening parenthesis and the capital A. It is comma-shaped, rather than a round full stop.

decisions.place: Third entry, N with raised underlined o
decisions.scan_shows: The o is raised and has a short separate horizontal line below it; it is not only a degree-circle form.

decisions.place: Fourth entry, abbreviation before les constructions
decisions.scan_shows: Two tall t strokes lead directly into a compressed e-s ending; there is no intervening ou sequence.
S-y-s-t and the grave-accent stroke can be followed. The last joined e/s portion is a low extended line with a small downward end, insufficient to decide singular or plural from the ink alone.
The first small shape is a closed a loop, followed by the looped d, an i trace, the round q with descender, and the u-e-s continuation. No separate leading hyphen precedes the a.
The apparent opening parenthesis continues as one unbroken long stroke beneath the inserted adiques and turns upward at the far right; it is the insertion connector, not a parenthesis before dans.
The initial looped d and final looped s are visible, but the middle pale strokes and accent marks remain compressed and partly merged with the graph-paper ruling. The tentative word is retained.

decisions.place: Below the parenthetical placement note, left faint mark
decisions.scan_shows: A short low left stroke rises slightly, bends down, then turns into a longer rising right stroke. It has no secure letter or word reading and is reproduced as a faint mark.

decisions.place: Below the parenthetical placement note, central faint mark
decisions.scan_shows: A very pale angular cluster has an upright segment, two oblique lower branches, and short separate traces below. It does not support a verbal reading; the reading preserves an uncertain graphic approximation.

decisions.place: Right of the space below (ou dans thèse)
decisions.scan_shows: Two separate dark round marks run from lower left to upper right. Their oblique separation is certain; whether they constitute authorial punctuation is not. They are retained graphically.

decisions.place: Sixth entry, word after introduction du
decisions.scan_shows: The crop shows one tall initial downstroke with a long low return, a faint second upright, a rounded middle bend, and a reduced final wave. These favour livre but do not securely separate every letter from the H-o-m possibility.

The right edge contains a rounded upright continuation after expo, a low final stroke, and a long rising accent-like stroke. The ending has ink and is not silently supplied, but its reduced s/e joins remain uncertain.
No detached low comma follows the terminal word strokes at the right edge before the next line starts with signaler.
After the l/apostrophe there is a run of low arches ending in a short i with a detached dot. No p descender occurs in the word.
The t ascender, short r, round o, and descending p are distinct in the right half; the word can be read without H doubt.

The raised glyph descends from its upper-left start to a lower bend and then rises on the right. It has the v-shaped stroke order of nu, not the arch of n. The separate slash and looped ell are also visible.

decisions.place: Sixth entry, marks before closing coefficient parenthesis
decisions.scan_shows: The right half shows two separated short horizontal marks after the final Z and before the closing parenthesis; a third point is not present.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, separator after i
decisions.scan_shows: Two heavy angular lobes are separated vertically, with a much lighter trace near their left edges. Their small scale prevents deciding a colon against an angular or membership-like joined mark; the arrow is separately right-pointing.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, generic-point glyph after separator
decisions.scan_shows: A short left upright joins a rounded shoulder and a long right descender curving left below the line. Eta is favoured, but the loop form also admits y; the recurring ambiguity is marked here.
The small t with its crossing stroke sits substantially above the baseline of the p and to its upper right. The raised placement is preserved.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, comma after générique
decisions.scan_shows: A short detached low oblique stroke appears after the final e of générique, at the end of the first line; it is kept as the comma.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, subscript on F
decisions.scan_shows: The lowered glyph has a short left arm, a rounded rise, and a long right descender sweeping left. It repeats the eta/y ambiguity first marked after i; the F itself has a single stem and two bars.
After the clear loc. the word has a tall looped l and a second tall b-like stroke, but the intervening i and final r/e run are reduced. Libre is retained with a local doubt.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, isolated glyph after sur
decisions.scan_shows: The isolated glyph repeats the short left arm and curved descending right stroke seen in the first occurrence. It is rendered eta under the first-occurrence ambiguity convention, without asserting a new resolution.

decisions.place: Last prose entry, punctuation after isolated generic-point glyph
decisions.scan_shows: There is no separate comma to the right of the isolated glyph. Its long low leftward tail belongs to the glyph itself.
This lowered form has a particularly visible rounded arch and long hooked right descender. It supports eta while the page-wide eta/y identity remains conservatively marked at the first occurrence.
A short left upright and rounded shoulder lead into the long left-turning right descender; this is the same recurring eta/y form, rendered with the first candidate.

notes: One wholly handwritten graph-paper sheet containing seven entries: weak Lefschetz without assuming X or Y smooth; a Q-ell sheaf definition in terms of champ associé; restating SGA 4 notions in Z-ell/Q-ell sheaf language; constructions in the relatively smooth case; adic projective systems in derived categories with the separate alternative-placement note (ou dans thèse); concern about overly particular coefficients; and a requested duality formula for the inclusion of the generic point. The page is a list of tasks or proposals, not a written proof of those claims. Explicit authorial openness is expressed by Essayer de faire and by (ou dans thèse); the cancelled exposé number and inserted adiques are also retained. There is no separate overall title, no date, and no authorial manuscript page number identified on this sheet. The visible 51 at bottom left is treated only as the archive number, consistent with the packet; the scan identifier is 52 and the cote marker is 37. Body handwriting attribution is left unnamed because the assigned packet does not independently establish authorship. Two horizontal rules, the numeral rules, the VI enclosing stroke, the adiques connector, two faint isolated marks, and the oblique right-hand dot pair are included. Every requested source image was viewed once in whole/a/b order; every listed crop was viewed once. Macro-only witness differences and H editorial prose describing the paper were not counted as transcription disagreements. No mathematical proof, computation, or external-background check was performed. Administrative validation passed for JSON, decision kinds, bboxes, paths, single-backslash LaTeX strings, and balanced TeX braces. A pdflatex compile was attempted, but the installed engine could not find pdflatex.fmt and stopped before reading the document; this is not a completed compilation check.
math_reading_decisions: The extra strokes in Q and Z support blackboard/double-stroke capitals; the lowered loop is ell, and D and F remain ordinary single-stem capitals.
The coefficient exponent has a descending left branch and an ascending right branch; it is read as nu, without replacing it by an expected n.
Two short horizontal marks after the final coefficient Z are kept as two dashes rather than normalized to an ellipsis.
The separator after i remains colon/less-than/membership ambiguous; the inclusion wording was not used to force a colon.
The generic-point glyph is retained as eta/y at its first occurrence. The four repetitions are rendered eta under the supplied recurring-glyph convention; each has its own crop and decision.
The final formula retains both inner pairs of parentheses, equality, and the two lower star subscripts on i exactly as visible.
The point abbreviation has a raised t and is transcribed as p with superscript t, not as a mathematical exponent to be interpreted.
The long stroke before dans belongs to the adiques insertion connector; no extra opening parenthesis is introduced there.

completion: Complete independent diplomatic reading of scan 052: all seven text entries, the display, visible deletions and insertions, underlining/rules, connecting strokes, faint isolated marks, marginal dots, and archive-number comment are covered. All fifteen C doubt locations (including the recurring-glyph entry) have explicit decisions; all observed substantive C/H disagreements and new uncertainties have whole-image bboxes. The three supplied source images and twenty-three unique one-per-open-place crops were each viewed once. No other reader, page, OCR, published text, or external source was consulted.
